NTA & Procedural Information Decoder

Understand Your Notice to Appear.

This tool explains a sample Notice to Appear, also called an NTA. Keep your own NTA nearby so you can compare its sections with the sample. Select a highlighted section to learn what it means and what information you may need to verify.

Your document may have a different layout, wording, or additional pages. This sample cannot explain every situation. If something differs or is unclear, ask an immigration lawyer or DOJ-accredited representative.

This is an educational support tool. It does not provide legal advice or replace help from a qualified legal professional.

You do not need to upload your NTA or share your name, A-number, address, or other identifying information to use this tool.

Sample for learning—this is not your case information.
Official blank Form I-862 (6/22). Click a highlighted area. The linked official sample is blank; your completed NTA will contain information specific to you.
